## Confirmed root cause

Three separate defects combine to corrupt post-FX:

1. Guest MSAA is decoded incorrectly.

   `RB_SURFACE_INFO.msaa_samples` occupies bits 16–17, but both native paths mask the lower halfword:

   - Definition: [registers.h](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/include/rex/graphics/registers.h:669)
   - Hook bug: [gta4_native_hooks.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/gta4-recomp/src/gta4_native_hooks.cpp:1587)
   - Renderer bug: [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:1967)

   Correctly decoded, `00800050` is a 1× surface and `00420028` is a 4× surface. The logs currently report both as `s0`.

2. The hook skips the game’s default resolve-sample normalization.

   The generated `sub_82A3CC68` chooses a default selector from the source MSAA mode when the caller leaves the selector field unset: [gta4_recomp.80.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/gta4-recomp/generated/gta4_recomp.80.cpp:68484). The native hook intercepts before that code and submits the original flags directly: [gta4_native_hooks.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/gta4-recomp/src/gta4_native_hooks.cpp:3223).

   Therefore logged zero selector bits do not mean “sample zero.” For the observed 4× views, stock behavior selects the complete multisample result.

3. The renderer tracks content per `VkImage`, while the game tracks content by guest placement.

   The trace shows valid 1× surfaces followed by unwritten 4× views at half dimensions:

   - Full-resolution → half-resolution: [Liberty Recompiled_401.10.log](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty%20Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty%20Recompiled_401.10.log:2133)
   - Luminance → half-size luminance: [same log](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty%20Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty%20Recompiled_401.10.log:2155)
   - Small luminance → smaller 4× view: [same log](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty%20Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty%20Recompiled_401.10.log:2177)

   In Xenos sample-space these are alternate views of the same logical placement, not independent empty resources. Xenia’s verified mapping expands 4× samples across both axes: [edram.xesli](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/tools/xenia-master-1/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/edram.xesli:23).

   The renderer copies those isolated, unwritten images anyway. Nonfinite data is then visible before the final shader consumes it: [Liberty Recompiled_401.10.log](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty%20Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty%20Recompiled_401.10.log:3172).

Resolve clears prove the same underlying ownership defect. A clear is requested but only logged as unapplied: [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:7553). The next surface view loads stale content because `ever_written` belongs to its host image, not the current guest placement: [Liberty Recompiled_411.log](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty%20Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty%20Recompiled_411.log:4144).

This is also why the cached attachment descriptor becomes stale: `SurfaceDescriptorsEqual` deliberately ignores placement, yet the cached image retains its old descriptor: [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:1031).

## Proper implementation

1. Correct and centralize descriptor decoding.

   Introduce typed helpers for:

   - `surface_info_word`
   - guest MSAA
   - color/depth placement base
   - format and aspect
   - normalized guest sample-space pitch and region

   Commands must carry their captured descriptor. Never derive current placement from the cached image descriptor.

2. Normalize resolve selectors exactly like generated code.

   Before recording a native resolve:

   - Apply the generated 1×/2×/4× default-selection behavior.
   - Preserve explicit selectors.
   - Sanitize selector/MSAA/depth combinations using the existing verified rules: [draw_util.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/util/draw.cpp:686).

3. Add logical placement ownership metadata.

   This is not physical EDRAM emulation. It is metadata mapping guest placement regions to their newest valid host representation.

   Each write, clear, view materialization and resolve-clear gets a monotonic serial. Before any attachment `LOAD` or resolve read, the renderer finds the newest owner of that guest region and materializes the requested view if necessary. `ever_written` remains only Vulkan image-initialization state.

4. Use programmable guest-sample-space conversion.

   The current shader blindly averages every sample: [resolve_convert_msaa_ps.glsl](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/resolve_convert_msaa_ps.glsl:3). Replace that behavior with explicit Xenos selectors and mappings, using integer-coordinate `texelFetch`.

   This is required because Vulkan’s built-in resolve:

   - Has no Xenos sample-selector argument.
   - Uses implementation-dependent behavior for float and normalized formats.
   - Requires matching source/destination formats.

   See the official [`vkCmdResolveImage` specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdResolveImage.html) and [`texelFetch` multisample overload](https://docs.vulkan.org/glsl/latest/chapters/builtinfunctions.html#texelfetch).

   Literal Vulkan memory aliasing is unsuitable: `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_ALIAS_BIT` only guarantees consistent interpretation for images with identical creation parameters, while these views differ in dimensions and sample count. [Vulkan image alias documentation](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImageCreateFlagBits.html).

5. Implement resolve-clear as an ordered placement write.

   Resolve copy and source clear must be separate operations. The clear must execute after the copy attempt whenever requested, including when the destination copy is rejected. Full clears can directly replace ownership; partial clears must preserve outside content and then clear the exact rectangle. Vulkan explicitly supports rectangular attachment clears through [`vkCmdClearAttachments`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdClearAttachments.html).

This fix is independent of HDR, shader overrides and reflection phase. High-resolution/native features exposed the invalid assumptions, but the failing trace is a non-reflection composite pass and corruption exists before the final shader. No codebase files were changed during this research.

Those NaNs entered deferred lighting and poisoned the final composite. # Static Recompilation System Prompt

## Core Principle
You're translating console code to run on different hardware. One fundamental distinction matters:

**Hardware-bound code** → Stub it (waiting for non-existent hardware causes hangs/corruption)
**Game logic code** → Implement it fully (this is the actual game)

## Hardware vs Logic: Ask One Question
"Does this code expect a physical device to respond?"

**YES (Stub these):**
- GPU command buffers expecting hardware ACKs
- DMA engines, MMIO registers, kernel interrupts
- Xbox OS-specific thread scheduling

**NO (Implement these):**
- Gameplay, physics, AI, animations
- Camera systems, rendering calculations
- Any code that processes data from other game code

## Python for ALL Math: Non-Negotiable

Every mathematical calculation uses Python scripts. No exceptions.

**Why:** In systems programming, math errors cause architectural catastrophes:
- Off-by-one → memory corruption hours later in unrelated systems
- Wrong pointer arithmetic → GPU overwrites audio buffers
- Alignment errors → silent command stream rejection

**Use Python for:**
- All hex arithmetic (address + offset)
- All pointer arithmetic, bit operations
- All size/alignment/buffer calculations
- All coordinate/matrix math
- All timing calculations

**No exceptions for** "simple additions" or "obvious" multiplications. Human brains fail at hex arithmetic, operator precedence, and overflow detection. You won't get a second chance.
 
## Implementation Completeness

No TODOs or stubs in logic code. Partial implementations create silent failures that compound into untraceable bugs. Complete implementations only—your code review is the only review.

## Trust Model
- ✅ Trust Hex-Rays for behavioral understanding
- ❌ Don't trust it for architecture/design recovery  
- ❌ Don't trust yourself for arithmetic without Python

## Project Structure
- **Recompiled source code (our binary):** `/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/LibertyRecompLib/ppc`
- **IDA Pro pseudocode (original binary):** `/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/gta_iv/default (1).xex.c` - useful for understanding rough structure

Problem Statement\n  * 2. Solution Space\n  * 3. Proposal\n    * 3.1. New Vulkan feature\n    * 3.2. New SPIR-V Execution Modes\n    * 3.3. New GLSL Layout Qualifiers\n    * 3.4. New HLSL Attributes\n  * 4. Issues\n    * 4.1. Should we expose a property indicating if the implementation is actually going to perform early and late tests?\n\nThis document describes a proposal for a new SPIR-V execution mode that allows fragment shaders to be discarded by early fragment operations, even if they contain writes to storage resources or other side effects.\n\n## 1. Problem Statement\n\nMost graphics devices are able to take advantage of early fragment operations when a fragment shader avoids certain operations - e.g. writing to depth or stencil, or to storage resources, providing significant performance advantages in most cases. This is implicitly enabled wherever possible, and can be explicitly enabled by specifying the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode in SPIR-V. However the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode makes it invalid to write fragment depth from a shader.\n\nSome implementations can perform depth testing both before and after fragment shading, allowing a conservative early test to discard most fragments and a late test to discard with more precision. GL_ARB_conservative_depth added a way to enable this optimization even when depth was written by the fragment shader, allowing further optimizations to be achieved in certain conditions. However, if the shader also writes to storage resources, no such optimization is possible due to the predictability requirements of the specification. In cases where an application does not care whether storage writes are performed by a fragment shader when discarded, it is possible to use this capability for a significant performance improvement on some console platforms, but so far Vulkan has no mechanism to do this. For some applications, this can mean an unnecessary performance hit that should be relatively straightforward to solve.\n## 3. Proposal\n\n### 3.1. New Vulkan feature\n    \n    `typedef struct VkPhysicalDeviceShaderEarlyAndLateFragmentTestsFeaturesAMD {\n        VkStructureType    sType;\n        void*              pNext;\n        VkBool32           shaderEarlyAndLateFragmentTests;\n    } VkPhysicalDeviceShaderEarlyAndLateFragmentTestsFeaturesAMD;`\n\nThis feature allows the new execution mode in SPIR-V shaders consumed by the implementation.\n\n### 3.2. New SPIR-V Execution Modes\n\nA new execution mode is introduced which allows for early depth and stencil tests to be performed both early and late when depth and stencil writes are performed, in combination with the depth optimizations. In order to allow for stencil reference writes with this new execution mode, similar stencil reference write optimizations are provided.\n\nExecution mode  | Extra Operands  | Enabling Capabilities\n--- | --- | ---\n5017  | EarlyAndLateFragmentTestsAMD\nFragment tests can be performed both before and after fragment shader execution, with latter tests taking values written to FragDepth and FragStencilRefEXT into account. Early tests are not guaranteed, late tests are.+\nIf neither of ExecutionModeDepthReplacing or ExecutionModeStencilRefReplacingEXT are specified, functions identically to EarlyFragmentTests.\nIf this and ExecutionModeStencilRefReplacingEXT are both specified, one of StencilRefGreaterAMD, StencilRefLessAMD, or StencilRefUnchangedAMD must also be specified.\nIf this and ExecutionModeDepthReplacing are both specified, one of DepthGreater, DepthLess, or DepthUnchanged must also be specified.\nOnly valid with the Fragment Execution Model.\nSee client API for detail on fragment operations.  |  | Shader\n5079  | StencilRefUnchangedFrontAMD\nIndicates that early per-fragment tests may assume that any FragStencilRefEXT built in-decorated value written by the shader is equal to the stencil reference value set for the front face in the client API after masking. Late per-fragment tests will use the written value as normal.\nOnly valid with the Fragment Execution Model.\nImplementations are allowed to perform optimizations assuming that the stencil test fails (or passes) for a given fragment if all values of `gl_FragStencilRefARB` consistent with the declaration would fail (or pass). This potentially includes skipping shader execution if the fragment is discarded because it is occluded and the shader has no side effects. If the final value of `gl_FragStencilRefARB` is inconsistent with the declaration for the facing of the shaded polygon, the result of the stencil test for the corresponding fragment is undefined. If the stencil test passes and stencil writes are enabled, the value written to the stencil buffer is always the value of `gl_FragStencilRefARB`, whether or not it is consistent with the layout qualifier.\n\nEach of the above qualifiers maps directly to the equivalently named spir-v execution mode.\n\n### 3.4. New HLSL Attributes\n\nThe following new Vulkan Specific Attribute is added:\n\n  * `early_and_late_tests`: Marks an entry point as enabling early and late depth tests. If depth is written via `SV_Depth`, `depth_unchanged` must also be specified (SV_DepthLess and SV_DepthGreater can be written freely). If a stencil reference value is written via `SV_StencilRef`, one of `stencil_ref_unchanged_front`, `stencil_ref_greater_equal_front`, or `stencil_ref_less_equal_front` and one of `stencil_ref_unchanged_back`, `stencil_ref_greater_equal_back`, or `stencil_ref_less_equal_back` must be specified.\n\n  * `depth_unchanged`: Specifies that any depth written to `SV_Depth` will not invalidate the result of early depth tests. Sets the `DepthUnchanged` execution mode in SPIR-V.\n\n  * `stencil_ref_unchanged_front`: Specifies that any stencil ref written to `SV_StencilRef` will not invalidate the result of early stencil tests when the fragment is front facing. These operations are defined as interlocked operations. How interlocked operations are ordered against other fragment shader invocations depends on the specified execution modes.\n\nIf the `ShadingRateInterlockOrderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute later in rasterization order and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area, and must happen after interlocked operations in a fragment shader that executes earlier in rasterization order and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area.\n## Representative Fragment Test\n\nThe representative fragment test allows implementations to reduce the amount of rasterization and fragment processing work performed for each point, line, or triangle primitive. This is implicitly enabled wherever possible, and can be explicitly enabled by specifying the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode in SPIR-V. However the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode makes it invalid to write fragment depth from a shader.\n\nSome implementations can perform depth testing both before and after fragment shading, allowing a conservative early test to discard most fragments and a late test to discard with more precision. However, if the shader also writes to storage resources, no such optimization is possible due to the predictability requirements of the specification. In cases where an application does not care whether storage writes are performed by a fragment shader when discarded, it is possible to use this capability for a significant performance improvement on some console platforms, but so far Vulkan has no mechanism to do this. ## 🤖 Agent

Research complete; no code edits, Git, or pseudocode used.

### Strongest findings

1. Native alpha-test semantics are incomplete and can contaminate depth.

The native path enables shader alpha testing only for `GreaterEqual` in [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:6064). Live glass draws request `alpha=1:5:0`; enum value 5 is `NotEqual` in [xenos.h](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/include/rex/graphics/xenos.h:677).

The established shared renderer supports all comparison functions, including a dedicated NotEqual implementation, in [spirv_translator_rb.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/pipeline/shader/spirv_translator_rb.cpp:490), with the guest function passed through in [command_processor.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/vulkan/command_processor.cpp:6308).

This is a proven parity defect. Because affected glass draws also use depth writes, transparent texels that should be discarded can write depth and over-occlude later glass and light sprites.

2. Water is submitted, but the sampled framebuffer probe does not change.

The active trace identifies water PS `C64FD3C169FB7A5A` as `water_e2` via [shader_cache.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/LibertyRecompLib/shader/shader_cache.cpp:1051). Its live state is conventional alpha blending, reverse-depth `Greater`, depth write enabled, stencil `NotEqual`, and RT0 mask `0xF`.

In frame 10560, multiple water checkpoints retained the same sampled-grid checksum, for example observed at `Liberty Recompiled_437.3.log:2209-2227`. This means the probe’s sampled pixels saw no change; it is not a whole-image proof. The new occlusion query will provide the decisive full-draw zero/nonzero coverage result.

3. The recent opaque-light occlusion fix feeds both symptom families.

The explicit recent fix is the combined sample-zero depth/stencil resolve described in [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:7759). Execution logs show:

`source=40226600 destination=D9132320 mode=sample-zero depth=true stencil=true`

Water binds `D9132320` at texture stage 2. The water shader family defines stage 2 as `DepthBufferSampler` and samples it in [water_ps1_smooth_shorelines.hlsl](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/LibertyRecompLib/shader_overrides/water/water_ps1_smooth_shorelines.hlsl:1217). Light sprites bind the same texture at stage 16, while retail metadata independently identifies `LightOcclusionTex` in [all_strings_with_addrs.txt](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/gta_iv/xex_excavation_retail/all_strings_with_addrs.txt:12012).

Therefore the resolved scene depth is a direct common coupling:

- If water/light occlusion queries return zero, fixed depth/stencil/cull rejected all coverage.
- If they return nonzero while the RT probe remains unchanged, shader output or alpha is zero; resolved-depth sampling becomes the leading cause.

4. Attachment depth lineage is not yet proven.

Opaque rendering uses multisampled depth `40226600`; later water, glass, and light sprites directly depth-test single-sample `400007C0`, both at guest address `00010000`. Placement keys include sample-space dimensions in [surface_view.h](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/include/rex/graphics/gta4_native/surface_view.h:23), so these become separate owners. When no exact owner is found, [PrepareSurfaceContent](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:8226) silently accepts the existing image.

This is a strong lineage risk, not yet proven as the rendering root. Also, `ClaimSurfaceContent` records a successful write whenever a draw was recorded and write state was enabled—even if every sample failed—so current write serials do not prove actual GPU coverage.

### Lower-priority parity gaps

- Native applies one blend state and the low color-mask nibble to every attachment in [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:5989). The shared renderer selects independent blend state and mask nibble per RT in [pipeline_cache.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:1553). This is real MRT divergence, but observed failing draws target RT0 with mask `0xF`.
- Native unknown blend factors default to `ONE`; shared Xenia maps unknown values, including 2 and 3, to zero in [pipeline_cache.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:1304). Observed failing draws use supported factors 6/7, so this is not the current cause.
- The active water hash is `water_e2`, not the new `water_ps1` override hash `C3256D6D7C2E426D` in [manifest.json](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/LibertyRecompLib/shader_overrides/manifest.json:96). The shoreline override is not causing these water draws to disappear.

### Required deterministic records

The new occlusion-query instrumentation is the correct next discriminator. Extend it with:

- At fixed-state decode/pipeline creation: raw packed words, cull mode/front face, alpha requested/supported/specialized, actual Vulkan blend/mask per attachment.
- At dynamic stencil setup: two-sided flag; front/CCW fail, depth-fail, pass, compare ops; front/back reference, compare mask, and write mask; effective Vulkan front/back state.
- Immediately after the `D9132320` resolve and before the first water/light/glass draw: deterministic depth min/max/checksum and stencil histogram.
- For each classified draw: occlusion samples passed plus target probe before/after. Use shader filename categories, not hard-coded hashes.
- Log `placement-no-exact-owner` at the current silent return when the same address exists under another sample-space key.

Vulkan confirms that stencil/depth failures clear sample coverage, occlusion queries count samples passing per-fragment tests, and blend/write masks are per attachment: [Fragment Operations](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/fragops.html), [Queries](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/queries.html), [Color Blend Attachment State](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPipelineColorBlendAttachmentState.html).

## 🤖 Agent

The generator confirms the coupling: every pixel shader gets a specialization-controlled `clip`, yet every shader that does not export depth is also unconditionally marked early-depth. That combination is architecturally unsafe for alpha-tested draws with depth writes; I’m now mapping the cache-generation path and the exact comparison encoding needed across both generated shaders and overrides.

In some cases, the representative fragment test may not discard any fragments for a given primitive.\n\n# Fragment Operations\n\nFragments produced by rasterization go through a number of operations to determine whether or how values produced by fragment shading are written to the framebuffer.\n\nThe following fragment operations adhere to rasterization order, and are typically performed in this order:\n\n  1. Discard rectangles test\n\n  2. Scissor test\n\n  3. Exclusive scissor test\n\n  4. Sample mask test\n\n  5. Certain Fragment shading operations:\n\n     * Sample Mask Accesses\n\n     * Tile Image Reads\n\n     * Depth Replacement\n\n     * Stencil Reference Replacement\n\n     * Interlocked Operations\n\n  6. Multisample coverage\n\n  7. Depth bounds test\n\n  8. Stencil test\n\n  9. Depth test\n\n  10. Representative fragment test\n\n  11. Sample counting\n\n  12. Coverage to color\n\n  13. Coverage reduction\n\n  14. Coverage modulation\n\nThe coverage mask generated by rasterization describes the initial coverage of each sample covered by the fragment. Fragment operations will update the coverage mask to add or subtract coverage where appropriate. If a fragment operation results in all bits of the coverage mask being `0`, the fragment is discarded, and no further operations are performed.\n\nWhen one of the fragment operations in this chapter is described as “replacing” a fragment shader output, that output is replaced unconditionally, even if no fragment shader previously wrote to that output.\n\nIf there is a fragment shader and it declares the `PostDepthCoverage` execution mode, the sample mask test is instead performed after the depth test.\n\nIf `VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance5Properties`::`earlyFragmentMultisampleCoverageAfterSampleCounting` is VK_TRUE and there is a fragment shader which declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, fragment shading and multisample coverage operations must be performed after sample counting.\n\nOtherwise, if fragment shading and multisample coverage operations should instead be performed after sample counting, but may be performed before sample counting.\n\nIf In cases where an application does not care whether storage writes are performed by a fragment shader when discarded, it is possible to use this capability for a significant performance improvement on some console platforms, but so far Vulkan has no mechanism to do this. If the bit in \ue200cite\ue20268†VkPipelineMultisampleStateCreateInfo\ue201 ::`pSampleMask` which is associated with that same sample index is set to `0`, the coverage mask bit is set to `0`.\nL664: ## Fragment Shading\nL665: \nL666: \ue200cite\ue20273†Fragment shaders\ue201 are invoked for each fragment, or as \ue200cite\ue20274†helper invocations\ue201 .\nL667: \nL668: Most operations in the fragment shader are not performed in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 , with exceptions called out in the following sections.\nL669: \nL670: For fragment shaders invoked by fragments, the following rules apply:\nL671: \nL672:   * A fragment shader must not be executed if a \ue200cite\ue20275†fragment operation\ue201 that executes before fragment shading discards the fragment.\nL673: \nL674:   * A fragment shader may not be executed if:\nL675:     * An implementation determines that another fragment shader, invoked by a subsequent primitive in \ue200cite\ue20276†primitive order\ue201 , overwrites all results computed by the shader (including writes to storage resources).\nL676: \nL677:     * Any other \ue200cite\ue20275†fragment operation\ue201 discards the fragment, and the shader does not write to any storage resources.\nL678:     * If a fragment shader statically computes the same values for different framebuffer locations, and does not write to any storage resources, multiple fragments may be shaded by one fragment shader invocation. This may affect \ue200cite\ue20277†VK_QUERY_PIPELINE_STATISTIC_FRAGMENT_SHADER_INVOCATIONS_BIT\ue201 results, but must otherwise not be visible behavior to applications.\nL679: \nL680:   * Otherwise, at least one fragment shader must be executed.\nL681:     * If \ue200cite\ue20278†sample shading\ue201 is enabled and multiple invocations per fragment are required, additional invocations must be executed as specified.\nL682: \nL683:     * If a \ue200cite\ue20279†shading rate image\ue201 is used and multiple invocations per fragment are required, additional invocations must be executed as specified.\nL684: \nL685:     * Each covered sample must be included in at least one fragment shader invocation.\nL686: If no fragment shader is included in the pipeline, no fragment shader is executed, and undefined values may be written to all color attachment outputs during this fragment operation.\nL687:  | Multiple fragment shader invocations may be executed for the same fragment for any number of implementation-dependent reasons. When there is more than one fragment shader invocation per fragment, the association of samples to invocations is implementation-dependent. Stores and atomics performed by these additional invocations have the normal effect. For example, if the subpass includes multiple views in its view mask, a fragment shader may be invoked separately for each view.\nL688: Similarly, if the render pass has a fragment density map attachment, more than one fragment shader invocation may be invoked for each covered sample. Such additional invocations are only produced if `VkPhysicalDeviceFragmentDensityMapPropertiesEXT`::`fragmentDensityInvocations` is \ue200cite\ue20230†VK_TRUE\ue201 . Implementations may generate these additional fragment shader invocations in order to make transitions between fragment areas with different fragment densities more smooth.\nL689: ### Sample Mask\nL690: \nL691: Reading from the \ue200cite\ue20280†`SampleMask`\ue201 built-in in the `Input` storage class will return the coverage mask for the current fragment as calculated by fragment operations that executed prior to fragment shading.\nL692: \nL693: If \ue200cite\ue20278†sample shading\ue201 is enabled, fragment shaders will only see values of `1` for samples being shaded - other bits will be `0`.\nL694: Each bit of the coverage mask is associated with a sample index as described in the \ue200cite\ue20229†rasterization chapter\ue201 . If the bit in `SampleMask` which is associated with that same sample index is set to `0`, that coverage mask bit is set to `0`.\nL695: \nL696: Values written to the \ue200cite\ue20280†`SampleMask`\ue201 built-in in the `Output` storage class will be used by the \ue200cite\ue20220†multisample coverage\ue201 operation, with the same encoding as the input built-in.\nL697: ### Shader Termination and Demotion\nL698: \nL699: If a fragment shader is \ue200cite\ue20281†terminated early\ue201 or \ue200cite\ue20274†demoted to a helper invocation\ue201 by using `OpKill`, `OpTerminateInvocation`, or `OpDemoteToHelperInvocation`, samples covered by that shader invocation have their coverage mask bits set to `0`.\nL700: ### Fragment Shader Tile Image Reads\nL701: \nL702: If the `\ue200cite\ue20282†VK_EXT_shader_tile_image\ue201 ` extension is enabled, implementations divide the framebuffer into a grid of tiles. A \ue200cite\ue20283†tile image\ue201 is a view of a framebuffer attachment tile for fragments with locations within the tile.\nL703: \nL704: Within a render pass instance initiated by \ue200cite\ue20284†vkCmdBeginRenderingKHR\ue201 , fragment shader invocations can read the framebuffer color, depth, and stencil values at the fragment location via tile images.\nL705:  | Even though fragment shader invocation can only read from the corresponding fragment location, the abstraction of a tile image is introduced for the following reasons:\nL706: \nL707:   * Tile dimensions will be exposed in a future extension\nL708:   * Future functionality such as executing compute dispatches within render passes via tile shaders can leverage tile images.\nL709: Enabling \ue200cite\ue20285†shaderTileImageColorReadAccess\ue201 , \ue200cite\ue20286†shaderTileImageDepthReadAccess\ue201 , \ue200cite\ue20287†shaderTileImageStencilReadAccess\ue201 enables fragment shader invocations to read from color, depth, and stencil, respectively.\nL710: \nL711: Color values are read from tile image variables with `OpColorAttachmentReadEXT`. Tile image variables are linked to specific color attachments using `Location` decoration. See \ue200cite\ue20288†Fragment Tile Image Interface\ue201 for more details.\nL712: \nL713: Depth values are read with `OpDepthAttachmentReadEXT`.\nL714: Stencil values are read with `OpStencilAttachmentReadEXT`.\nL715: \nL716: The sample to read is specified by a \ue200cite\ue20229†sample index\ue201 value specified as the `Sample` operand to `OpColorAttachmentReadEXT`, `OpDepthAttachmentReadEXT`, or `OpStencilAttachmentReadEXT`.\nL717: If \ue200cite\ue20278†sample shading\ue201 is disabled, a fragment invocation can read from all sample locations associated with the fragment regardless of the fragment’s coverage. This functionality is supported for \ue200cite\ue20268†VkPipelineMultisampleStateCreateInfo\ue201 ::`rasterizationSamples` > 1 when \ue200cite\ue20289†VkPhysicalDeviceShaderTileImagePropertiesEXT\ue201 ::`shaderTileImageReadSampleFromPixelRateInvocation` is \ue200cite\ue20230†VK_TRUE\ue201 .\nL718: If \ue200cite\ue20278†sample shading\ue201 is enabled, and `minSampleShading` is 1.0, a fragment invocation must only read from the \ue200cite\ue20290†coverage index\ue201 sample. Tile image access must not be used if the value of `minSampleShading` is not 1.0.\nL719: \nL720: If the \ue200cite\ue20214†fragment shader\ue201 declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, depth reads are allowed only if depth writes are disabled and stencil reads are allowed only if stencil writes are disabled.\nL721: If \ue200cite\ue20289†VkPhysicalDeviceShaderTileImagePropertiesEXT\ue201 ::`shaderTileImageReadFromHelperInvocation` is \ue200cite\ue20231†VK_FALSE\ue201 , values read from helper invocations are poison, otherwise the values read are subject to the coherency guarantees described below.\nL722: \nL723: `OpDepthAttachmentReadEXT` returns a poison value if no depth attachment is present. `OpStencilAttachmentReadEXT` returns a poison value if no stencil attachment is present.\nL724: Tile image reads from color, depth, and stencil attachments are said to be coherent when the accesses happen in raster order and without \ue200cite\ue20291†data race\ue201 with respect to accesses to the attachments from framebuffer-space pipeline stages. The samples which qualify for coherent access and the enabling conditions are described below.\nL725: \nL726:   * Let Rc be the set of components being read from an attachment A in a draw call\nL727: \nL728:   * Let Wc be the set of components being written to A by the draw call\nL729: The samples which qualify for coherent tile image reads from an attachment A are:\nL730: \nL731:   * All samples in a pixel when Rc is disjoint with Wc.\nL732: \nL733:   * The samples with coverage in a fragment when Rc is not disjoint with Wc. The samples with coverage are determined by the coverage mask for the fragment as calculated by fragment operations that executed prior to fragment shading, including early fragment tests if enabled for the draw call.\nL734: A fragment shader can declare `NonCoherentColorAttachmentReadEXT`, `NonCoherentDepthAttachmentReadEXT`, or `NonCoherentStencilAttachmentReadEXT` execution modes to enable non-coherent tile image reads which require an explicit \ue200cite\ue20292†vkCmdPipelineBarrier2\ue201 call for the writes to an attachment to be made visible via tile image reads.\nL735: When \ue200cite\ue20289†VkPhysicalDeviceShaderTileImagePropertiesEXT\ue201 ::`shaderTileImageCoherentReadAccelerated` is \ue200cite\ue20230†VK_TRUE\ue201 , the implementation prefers that coherent tile image reads are used, otherwise the implementation prefers that non-coherent tile image reads are used.\nL736: \nL737:  | In practice, the most common tile image reads usage patterns fall under one of the following:\nL738:   * Programmable blending - each fragment reads from a single sample (SampleID) at its location. Per-sample shading is typically enabled when multisampled rendertargets are used.\nL739:   * G-buffer generation and shading in one render pass - in the shading phase a fragment reads from a single sample at its location.\nL740:   * Programmable resolve - a fragment reads from all samples at its location (per-sample shading is disabled). This requires the use of a “full-screen triangle” instead of a rectangle composed of two triangles in order to avoid data races along the shared edge of the triangles.\nL741:   * 1:1 texturing with LOD - in use cases such a deferred screen space decals a fragment reads a single sample (SampleID) from depth buffer, but requires being able to read from helper threads to derive the texture LOD. This use case is supported as long as the attachment components being read are not overwritten by color, depth, or stencil attachment writes.\nL742: All of the above use cases are supported by coherent tile image reads, but only the latter three are supported when non-coherent reads are used as there is no mechanism to synchronize non-coherent reads with writes within a draw call.\nL743: ### Depth Replacement\nL744: \nL745: Writing to the \ue200cite\ue20293†`FragDepth`\ue201 built-in will replace the fragment’s calculated depth values for each sample in the input `SampleMask`. \ue200cite\ue20223†Depth testing\ue201 performed after the fragment shader for this fragment will use this new value as z_{f}.\nL746: ### Stencil Reference Replacement\nL747: \nL748: Writing to the \ue200cite\ue20294†`FragStencilRefEXT`\ue201 built-in will replace the fragment’s stencil reference value for each sample in the input `SampleMask`. \ue200cite\ue20222†Stencil testing\ue201 performed after the fragment shader for this fragment will use this new value as s_{r}.\nL749: ### Interlocked Operations\nL750: \nL751: `OpBeginInvocationInterlockEXT` and `OpEndInvocationInterlockEXT` define a section of a fragment shader which imposes additional ordering constraints on operations performed within them. These operations are defined as interlocked operations. How interlocked operations are ordered against other fragment shader invocations depends on the specified execution modes.\nL752: If the `ShadingRateInterlockOrderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute later in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area, and must happen after interlocked operations in a fragment shader that executes earlier in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area.\nL753: If the `ShadingRateInterlockUnorderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before or after interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute earlier or later in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area.\nL754: If the `PixelInterlockOrderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute later in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one sample in the same pixel, and must happen after interlocked operations in a fragment shader that executes earlier in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one sample in the same pixel.\nL755: If the `PixelInterlockUnorderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before or after interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute earlier or later in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one sample in the same pixel.\nL756: If the `SampleInterlockOrderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute later in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one of the same samples, and must happen after interlocked operations in a fragment shader that executes earlier in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one of the same samples.\nL757: If the `SampleInterlockUnorderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before or after interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute earlier or later in \ue200cite\ue2029†rasterization order\ue201 and cover at least one of the same samples.\nL758: ## Multisample Coverage\nL759: If a fragment shader is active and its entry point’s interface includes a built-in output variable decorated with `SampleMask`, but not `OverrideCoverageNV`, the coverage mask is `ANDed` with the bits of the `SampleMask` built-in to generate a new coverage mask. If the `SampleMask` built-in is also decorated with `OverrideCoverageNV`, the coverage mask is replaced with the mask bits set in the shader.\nL760: If \ue200cite\ue20278†sample shading\ue201 is enabled, bits written to `SampleMask` corresponding to samples that are not being shaded by the fragment shader invocation are ignored. This consists of `rasterizationSamples` unique coverage samples for each pixel in the fragment area, each with a unique \ue200cite\ue20229†sample index\ue201 . Writing to the `FragDepth` built-in will replace the fragment’s calculated depth values for each sample in the input `SampleMask`. ...   * `depthWriteEnable` controls whether depth writes are enabled when `depthTestEnable` is VK_TRUE.\n\n# Fragment Operations\n\nFragments produced by rasterization go through a number of operations to determine whether or how values produced by fragment shading are written to the framebuffer.\n\nThe following fragment operations adhere to rasterization order, and are typically performed in this order:\n\n  1. Discard rectangles test\n\n  2. Scissor test\n\n  3. Exclusive scissor test\n\n  4. Sample mask test\n\n  5. Multisample coverage\n\n  7. Depth bounds test\n\n  8. Stencil test\n\n  9. Depth test\n\n  10. Representative fragment test\n\n  11. Sample counting\n\n  12. Coverage to color\n\n  13. Coverage reduction\n\n  14. Coverage modulation\n\nThe coverage mask generated by rasterization describes the initial coverage of each sample covered by the fragment. Fragment operations will update the coverage mask to add or subtract coverage where appropriate. If a fragment operation results in all bits of the coverage mask being `0`, the fragment is discarded, and no further operations are performed.\n\nWhen one of the fragment operations in this chapter is described as “replacing” a fragment shader output, that output is replaced unconditionally, even if no fragment shader previously wrote to that output.\n\nIf there is a fragment shader and it declares the `PostDepthCoverage` execution mode, the sample mask test is instead performed after the depth test.\n\nIf `VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance5Properties`::`earlyFragmentMultisampleCoverageAfterSampleCounting` is VK_TRUE and there is a fragment shader which declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, fragment shading and multisample coverage operations must be performed after sample counting.\n\nOtherwise, if `VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance5Properties`::`earlyFragmentMultisampleCoverageAfterSampleCounting` is VK_FALSE and there is a fragment shader which declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, fragment shading and multisample coverage operations should instead be performed after sample counting, but may be performed before sample counting.\n\nIf `VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance5Properties`::`earlyFragmentSampleMaskTestBeforeSampleCounting` is VK_TRUE and there is a fragment shader which declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode sample mask test operations must follow the order of fragment operations from above.\n\nOtherwise, if `VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance5Properties`::`earlyFragmentSampleMaskTestBeforeSampleCounting` is VK_FALSE and there is a fragment shader which declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, sample mask test operations should follow the order of fragment operations from above but may instead be performed after sample counting.\n\nIf there is a fragment shader which declares the `EarlyAndLateFragmentTestsAMD` execution mode, and it does not declare the `DepthReplacing` or `StencilRefReplacingEXT` execution mode, fragment shading and multisample coverage operations are instead be performed after sample counting.\n\nFor a pipeline with the following properties:\n\n  * a fragment shader is specified\n\n  * the fragment shader either specifies `EarlyAndLateFragmentTestsAMD` or does not write to storage resources;\n\n  * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefReplacingEXT` execution mode;\n\n  * either\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefUnchangedFrontAMD` execution mode;\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefLessFrontAMD` execution mode and the pipeline uses a VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`front.compareOp` of VK_COMPARE_OP_GREATER or VK_COMPARE_OP_GREATER_OR_EQUAL; or\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefGreaterFrontAMD` execution mode and the pipeline uses a VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`front.compareOp` of VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS or VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS_OR_EQUAL; and\n\n  * either\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefUnchangedBackAMD` execution mode;\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefLessBackAMD` execution mode and the pipeline uses a VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`back.compareOp` of VK_COMPARE_OP_GREATER or VK_COMPARE_OP_GREATER_OR_EQUAL; or\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `StencilRefGreaterBackAMD` execution mode and the pipeline uses a VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`back.compareOp` of VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS or VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS_OR_EQUAL\n\nan additional stencil test may be performed before fragment shading, using the stencil reference value specified by VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`front.reference` or VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`back.reference`.\n\nFor a pipeline with the following properties:\n\n  * a fragment shader is specified\n\n  * the fragment shader either specifies `EarlyAndLateFragmentTestsAMD` or does not write to storage resources;\n\n  * the fragment shader specifies the `DepthReplacing` execution mode; and\n\n  * either\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `DepthUnchanged` execution mode;\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `DepthLess` execution mode and the pipeline uses a VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthCompareOp` of VK_COMPARE_OP_GREATER or VK_COMPARE_OP_GREATER_OR_EQUAL; or\n\n    * the fragment shader specifies the `DepthGreater` execution mode and the pipeline uses a VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthCompareOp` of VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS or VK_COMPARE_OP_LESS_OR_EQUAL\n\nthe implementation may perform depth bounds test before fragment shading and perform an additional depth test immediately after that using the interpolated depth value generated by rasterization.\n\nOnce all fragment operations have completed, fragment shader outputs for covered color attachment samples pass through framebuffer operations.\n\n\n### Fragment Shader Tile Image Reads\n\nIf the `VK_EXT_shader_tile_image` extension is enabled, implementations divide the framebuffer into a grid of tiles. A tile image is a view of a framebuffer attachment tile for fragments with locations within the tile.\n\nWithin a render pass instance initiated by vkCmdBeginRenderingKHR, fragment shader invocations can read the framebuffer color, depth, and stencil values at the fragment location via tile images.\n\n | Even though fragment shader invocation can only read from the corresponding fragment location, the abstraction of a tile image is introduced for the following reasons:\n\n  * Tile dimensions will be exposed in a future extension\n  * Future functionality such as executing compute dispatches within render passes via tile shaders can leverage tile images.\n\nEnabling shaderTileImageColorReadAccess, shaderTileImageDepthReadAccess, shaderTileImageStencilReadAccess enables fragment shader invocations to read from color, depth, and stencil, respectively.\n\nColor values are read from tile image variables with `OpColorAttachmentReadEXT`. Tile image variables are linked to specific color attachments using `Location` decoration. See Fragment Tile Image Interface for more details.\n\nDepth values are read with `OpDepthAttachmentReadEXT`.\n\nStencil values are read with `OpStencilAttachmentReadEXT`.\n\nThe sample to read is specified by a sample index value specified as the `Sample` operand to `OpColorAttachmentReadEXT`, `OpDepthAttachmentReadEXT`, or `OpStencilAttachmentReadEXT`.\n\nIf sample shading is disabled, a fragment invocation can read from all sample locations associated with the fragment regardless of the fragment’s coverage. This functionality is supported for VkPipelineMultisampleStateCreateInfo::`rasterizationSamples` > 1 when VkPhysicalDeviceShaderTileImagePropertiesEXT::`shaderTileImageReadSampleFromPixelRateInvocation` is VK_TRUE.\n\nIf sample shading is enabled, and `minSampleShading` is 1.0, a fragment invocation must only read from the coverage index sample. Tile image access must not be used if the value of `minSampleShading` is not 1.0.\n\nIf the fragment shader declares the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, depth reads are allowed only if depth writes are disabled and stencil reads are allowed only if stencil writes are disabled.\n\nIf VkPhysicalDeviceShaderTileImagePropertiesEXT::`shaderTileImageReadFromHelperInvocation` is VK_FALSE, values read from helper invocations are poison, otherwise the values read are subject to the coherency guarantees described below.\n\n`OpDepthAttachmentReadEXT` returns a poison value if no depth attachment is present. `OpStencilAttachmentReadEXT` returns a poison value if no stencil attachment is present.\n\nTile image reads from color, depth, and stencil attachments are said to be coherent when the accesses happen in raster order and without data race with respect to accesses to the attachments from framebuffer-space pipeline stages. The samples which qualify for coherent access and the enabling conditions are described below.\n\n  * Let Rc be the set of components being read from an attachment A in a draw call\n\n  * Let Wc be the set of components being written to A by the draw call\n\nThe samples which qualify for coherent tile image reads from an attachment A are:\n\n  * All samples in a pixel when Rc is disjoint with Wc.\n\n  * The samples with coverage in a fragment when Rc is not disjoint with Wc. The samples with coverage are determined by the coverage mask for the fragment as calculated by fragment operations that executed prior to fragment shading, including early fragment tests if enabled for the draw call.\n\nA fragment shader can declare `NonCoherentColorAttachmentReadEXT`, `NonCoherentDepthAttachmentReadEXT`, or `NonCoherentStencilAttachmentReadEXT` execution modes to enable non-coherent tile image reads which require an explicit vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 call for the writes to an attachment to be made visible via tile image reads.\n\nWhen VkPhysicalDeviceShaderTileImagePropertiesEXT::`shaderTileImageCoherentReadAccelerated` is VK_TRUE, the implementation prefers that coherent tile image reads are used, otherwise the implementation prefers that non-coherent tile image reads are used.\n### Depth Replacement\n\nWriting to the `FragDepth` built-in will replace the fragment’s calculated depth values for each sample in the input `SampleMask`. Depth testing performed after the fragment shader for this fragment will use this new value as z_{f}.\n\n### Stencil Reference Replacement\n\nWriting to the `FragStencilRefEXT` built-in will replace the fragment’s stencil reference value for each sample in the input `SampleMask`. Stencil testing performed after the fragment shader for this fragment will use this new value as s_{r}.\n\n### Interlocked Operations\n\n`OpBeginInvocationInterlockEXT` and `OpEndInvocationInterlockEXT` define a section of a fragment shader which imposes additional ordering constraints on operations performed within them. These operations are defined as interlocked operations. How interlocked operations are ordered against other fragment shader invocations depends on the specified execution modes.\n\nIf the `ShadingRateInterlockOrderedEXT` execution mode is specified, any interlocked operations in a fragment shader must happen before interlocked operations in fragment shader invocations that execute later in rasterization order and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area, and must happen after interlocked operations in a fragment shader that executes earlier in rasterization order and cover at least one sample in the same fragment area.\n## Depth and Stencil Operations\n\nPipeline state controlling the depth bounds tests, stencil test, and depth test is specified through the members of the `VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo` structure.\n\nThe `VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo` structure is defined as:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_0\n    typedef struct VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo {\n        VkStructureType                           sType;\n        const void*                               pNext;\n        VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateFlags    flags;\n        VkBool32                                  depthTestEnable;\n        VkBool32                                  depthWriteEnable;\n        VkCompareOp                               depthCompareOp;\n        VkBool32                                  depthBoundsTestEnable;\n        VkBool32                                  stencilTestEnable;\n        VkStencilOpState                          front;\n        VkStencilOpState                          back;\n        float                                     minDepthBounds;\n        float                                     maxDepthBounds;\n    } VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo;`\n\n  * `sType` is a VkStructureType value identifying this structure.\n\n  * `pNext` is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this structure.\n\n  * `flags` is a bitmask of VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateFlagBits specifying additional depth/stencil state information.\n\n  * `depthTestEnable` controls whether depth testing is enabled.\n\n  * `depthWriteEnable` controls whether depth writes are enabled when `depthTestEnable` is VK_TRUE. Depth writes are always disabled when `depthTestEnable` is VK_FALSE.\n\n  * `depthCompareOp` is a VkCompareOp value specifying the comparison operator to use in the Depth Comparison step of the depth test.\n\n  * `depthBoundsTestEnable` controls whether depth bounds testing is enabled.\n\n  * `stencilTestEnable` controls whether stencil testing is enabled.\n\n  * `front` and `back` are VkStencilOpState values controlling the corresponding parameters of the stencil test.\n\n  * `minDepthBounds` is the minimum depth bound used in the depth bounds test.\n\n  * `maxDepthBounds` is the maximum depth bound used in the depth bounds test.\n\nValid Usage\n\n  * VUID-VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo-depthBoundsTestEnable-00598\nIf the `depthBounds` feature is not enabled, `depthBoundsTestEnable` must be VK_FALSE\n\n  * VUID-VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo-separateStencilMaskRef-04453\nIf the `VK_KHR_portability_subset` extension is enabled, and VkPhysicalDevicePortabilitySubsetFeaturesKHR::`separateStencilMaskRef` is VK_FALSE, and the value of VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`stencilTestEnable` is VK_TRUE, and the value of VkPipelineRasterizationStateCreateInfo::`cullMode` is VK_CULL_MODE_NONE, the value of `reference` in each of the VkStencilOpState structs in `front` and `back` must be the same\n\nWhen VK_PIPELINE_DEPTH_STENCIL_STATE_CREATE_RASTERIZATION_ORDER_ATTACHMENT_DEPTH_ACCESS_BIT_EXT is included in a pipeline, it forms a framebuffer-local memory dependency for each fragment generated by draw commands for that pipeline with the following scopes:\n\n  * The first synchronization scope includes VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_FRAGMENT_SHADER_BIT and VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT pipeline stages executed by all previous fragments (as defined by primitive order) in the corresponding framebuffer regions including those generated by the same draw command.\n\n  * The second synchronization scope includes VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_FRAGMENT_SHADER_BIT stage executed by the generated fragment.\n\n  * The first access scope includes all writes to the depth aspect of depth/stencil attachments.\n\n  * The second access scope includes all reads from the depth aspect of input attachments.\n\nWhen VK_PIPELINE_DEPTH_STENCIL_STATE_CREATE_RASTERIZATION_ORDER_ATTACHMENT_STENCIL_ACCESS_BIT_EXT is included in a pipeline, it forms a framebuffer-local memory dependency for each fragment generated by draw commands for that pipeline with the following scopes:\n\n  * The first synchronization scope includes VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_FRAGMENT_SHADER_BIT VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT pipeline stages executed by all previous fragments (as defined by primitive order) in the corresponding framebuffer regions including those generated by the same draw command.\n\n  * The second synchronization scope includes VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_FRAGMENT_SHADER_BIT and VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_LATE_FRAGMENT_TESTS_BIT pipeline stages executed by the generated fragment.\n\n  * The first access scope includes all writes to the stencil aspect of depth/stencil attachments.\n\n  * The second access scope includes all reads from the stencil aspect of input attachments.\n\n## Depth Bounds Test\n\nThe depth bounds test compares the depth value z_{a} in the depth/stencil attachment at each sample’s framebuffer coordinates (x_{f},y_{f}) and sample index i against a set of depth bounds.\n\nThe depth bounds are determined by two floating-point values defining a minimum (`minDepthBounds`) and maximum (`maxDepthBounds`) depth value. These values are either set by the VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo structure during pipeline creation, or dynamically by vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable and vkCmdSetDepthBounds.\n\nA given sample is considered within the depth bounds if z_{a} is in the range [`minDepthBounds`,`maxDepthBounds`]. Samples with depth attachment values outside of the depth bounds will have their coverage set to `0`.\n\nIf the depth bounds test is disabled, or if there is no depth attachment, the coverage mask is unmodified by this operation.\n\nTo dynamically enable or disable the depth bounds test, call:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_3\n    void vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkBool32                                    depthBoundsTestEnable);`\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state, VK_EXT_shader_object\n    // Equivalent to vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable\n    void vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnableEXT(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkBool32                                    depthBoundsTestEnable);`\n\n  * `commandBuffer` is the command buffer into which the command will be recorded.\n\n  * `depthBoundsTestEnable` specifies if the depth bounds test is enabled.\n\nThis command sets the depth bounds enable for subsequent drawing commands when drawing using shader objects, or when the graphics pipeline is created with VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_DEPTH_BOUNDS_TEST_ENABLE set in VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo::`pDynamicStates`. Otherwise, this state is specified by the VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthBoundsTestEnable` value used to create the currently active pipeline.\n\nValid Usage\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable-None-08971\nAt least one of the following must be true:\n\n    * the `extendedDynamicState` feature is enabled\n\n    * the `shaderObject` feature is enabled\n\n    * the value of VkApplicationInfo::`apiVersion` used to create the VkInstance parent of `commandBuffer` is greater than or equal to Version 1.3\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable-depthBounds-10010\nIf the `depthBounds` feature is not enabled, `depthBoundsTestEnable` must be VK_FALSE\n\nValid Usage (Implicit)\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable-commandBuffer-parameter\n`commandBuffer` must be a valid VkCommandBuffer handle\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable-commandBuffer-recording\n`commandBuffer` must be in the recording state\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable-commandBuffer-cmdpool\nThe `VkCommandPool` that `commandBuffer` was allocated from must support VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT operations\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthBoundsTestEnable-videocoding\n## Stencil Test\n\nThe stencil test compares the stencil attachment value s_{a} in the depth/stencil attachment at each sample’s framebuffer coordinates (x_{f},y_{f}) and sample index i against a stencil reference value.\n\nIf the render pass has a fragment density map attachment and the fragment covers multiple pixels, there is an implementation-dependent association of coverage samples to stencil attachment samples within the fragment. However, if all samples in the fragment are covered, and the stencil attachment value is updated as a result of this test, all stencil attachment samples will be updated.\n\nIf the stencil test is not enabled, as specified by vkCmdSetStencilTestEnable or VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`stencilTestEnable`, or if there is no stencil attachment, the coverage mask is unmodified by this operation.\n\nThe stencil test is controlled by one of two sets of stencil-related state, the front stencil state and the back stencil state. Stencil tests and writes use the back stencil state when processing fragments generated by back-facing polygons, and the front stencil state when processing fragments generated by front-facing polygons or any other primitives.\nIf the stencil test fails, `failOp` defines the stencil operation used. If the stencil test passes however, the stencil op used is based on the depth test - if it passes, VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`passOp` is used, otherwise VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthFailOp` is used.\n\nThe stencil attachment value s_{a} is then updated with the generated stencil value s_{g} according to the write mask s_{w} defined by `writeMask` in VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`front` and VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`back` as:\n\n    \n\ns_{a} = (s_{a} ∧ ¬s_{w}) ∨ (s_{g} ∧ s_{w})\n\nTo dynamically enable or disable the stencil test, call:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_3\n    void vkCmdSetStencilTestEnable(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkBool32                                    stencilTestEnable);`\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state, VK_EXT_shader_object\n    // Equivalent to vkCmdSetStencilTestEnable\n    void vkCmdSetStencilTestEnableEXT(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkBool32                                    stencilTestEnable);`\n\n  * `commandBuffer` is the command buffer into which the command will be recorded.\n\n  * `stencilTestEnable` specifies if the stencil test is enabled.\n\nThis command sets the stencil test enable for subsequent drawing commands when drawing using shader objects, or when the graphics pipeline is created with VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_STENCIL_TEST_ENABLE set in VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo::`pDynamicStates`. Otherwise, this state is specified by the VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`stencilTestEnable` value used to create the currently active pipeline.\n\nValid Usage\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetStencilTestEnable-None-08971\nAt least one of the following must be true:\n\n    * the `extendedDynamicState` feature is enabled\n\n    * the `shaderObject` feature is enabled\n\n--- | --- | --- | --- | ---\nPrimary\nSecondary  | Both  | Outside  | VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT  | State\n\nConditional Rendering\n\nvkCmdSetStencilTestEnable is not affected by conditional rendering\n\nTo dynamically set the stencil operation, call:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_3\n    void vkCmdSetStencilOp(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkStencilFaceFlags                          faceMask,\n        VkStencilOp                                 failOp,\n        VkStencilOp                                 passOp,\n        VkStencilOp                                 depthFailOp,\n        VkCompareOp                                 compareOp);`\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state, VK_EXT_shader_object\n    // Equivalent to vkCmdSetStencilOp\n    void vkCmdSetStencilOpEXT(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkStencilFaceFlags                          faceMask,\n        VkStencilOp                                 failOp,\n        VkStencilOp                                 passOp,\n        VkStencilOp                                 depthFailOp,\n        VkCompareOp                                 compareOp);`\n\n  * `commandBuffer` is the command buffer into which the command will be recorded.\n\n  * `faceMask` is a bitmask of VkStencilFaceFlagBits specifying the set of stencil state for which to update the stencil operation.\n\n  * `failOp` is a VkStencilOp value specifying the action performed on samples that fail the stencil test.\n\n  * `passOp` is a VkStencilOp value specifying the action performed on samples that pass both the depth and stencil tests.\n\n  * `depthFailOp` is a VkStencilOp value specifying the action performed on samples that pass the stencil test and fail the depth test.\n\n  * `compareOp` is a VkCompareOp value specifying the comparison operator used in the stencil test.\n\nThis command sets the stencil operation for subsequent drawing commands when when drawing using shader objects, or when the graphics pipeline is created with VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_STENCIL_OP set in VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo::`pDynamicStates`. \nConditional Rendering\n\nvkCmdSetStencilOp is not affected by conditional rendering\n\nThe `VkStencilOpState` structure is defined as:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_0\n    typedef struct VkStencilOpState {\n        VkStencilOp    failOp;\n        VkStencilOp    passOp;\n        VkStencilOp    depthFailOp;\n        VkCompareOp    compareOp;\n        uint32_t       compareMask;\n        uint32_t       writeMask;\n        uint32_t       reference;\n    } VkStencilOpState;`\n\n  * `failOp` is a VkStencilOp value specifying the action performed on samples that fail the stencil test.\n\n  * `passOp` is a VkStencilOp value specifying the action performed on samples that pass both the depth and stencil tests.\n\n  * `depthFailOp` is a VkStencilOp value specifying the action performed on samples that pass the stencil test and fail the depth test.\n\n  * `compareOp` is a VkCompareOp value specifying the comparison operator used in the stencil test.\n\n  * `compareMask` selects the bits of the unsigned integer stencil values participating in the stencil test.\n\n  * `writeMask` selects the bits of the unsigned integer stencil values updated by the stencil test in the stencil framebuffer attachment.\n\n  * `reference` is an integer stencil reference value that is used in the unsigned stencil comparison.\n\nValid Usage (Implicit)\n\n  * VUID-VkStencilOpState-failOp-parameter\n`failOp` must be a valid VkStencilOp value\n\n  * VUID-VkStencilOpState-passOp-parameter\n`passOp` must be a valid VkStencilOp value\n\n  * VUID-VkStencilOpState-depthFailOp-parameter\n`depthFailOp` must be a valid VkStencilOp value\n\n  * VUID-VkStencilOpState-compareOp-parameter\n`compareOp` must be a valid VkCompareOp value\n\nTo dynamically set the stencil compare mask, call:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_0\n    void vkCmdSetStencilCompareMask(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkStencilFaceFlags                          faceMask,\n        uint32_t                                    compareMask);`\n\n  * `commandBuffer` is the command buffer into which the command will be recorded.\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_0\n    void vkCmdSetStencilWriteMask(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkStencilFaceFlags                          faceMask,\n        uint32_t                                    writeMask);`\n\n  * `commandBuffer` is the command buffer into which the command will be recorded.\n\n  * `faceMask` is a bitmask of VkStencilFaceFlagBits specifying the set of stencil state for which to update the write mask, as described above for vkCmdSetStencilCompareMask.\n\n  * `writeMask` is the new value to use as the stencil write mask.\n\nThis command sets the stencil write mask for subsequent drawing commands when drawing using shader objects, or when the graphics pipeline is created with VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_STENCIL_WRITE_MASK set in VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo::`pDynamicStates`. Otherwise, this state is specified by the `writeMask` value used to create the currently active pipeline, for both VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`front` and VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`back` faces.\n## Depth Test\n\nThe depth test compares the depth value z_{a} in the depth/stencil attachment at each sample’s framebuffer coordinates (x_{f},y_{f}) and sample index i against the sample’s depth value z_{f}. If there is no depth attachment then the depth test is skipped.\n\nIf the render pass has a fragment density map attachment and the fragment covers multiple pixels, there is an implementation-dependent association of rasterization samples to depth attachment samples within the fragment. However, if all samples in the fragment are covered, and the depth attachment value is updated as a result of this test, all depth attachment samples will be updated.\n\nThe depth test occurs in three stages, as detailed in the following sections.\n\n### Depth Clamping and Range Adjustment\n\nIf VkPipelineRasterizationStateCreateInfo::`depthClampEnable` is enabled, z_{f} is clamped to [z_{min}, z_{max}], where z_{min} = min(n,f), z_{max} = max(n,f), and n and f are the `minDepth` and `maxDepth` depth range values of the viewport used by this fragment, respectively. ### Depth Comparison\n\nIf the depth test is not enabled, as specified by vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable or VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthTestEnable`, then this step is skipped.\n\nThe comparison operation performed is determined by the VkCompareOp value set by vkCmdSetDepthCompareOp, or by VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthCompareOp` during pipeline creation. z_{f} and z_{a} are used as the reference and test values, respectively, in the operation specified by the VkCompareOp.\n\nIf the comparison evaluates to false, the coverage for the sample is set to `0`.\n\n### Depth Attachment Writes\n\nIf depth writes are enabled, as specified by vkCmdSetDepthWriteEnable or VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthWriteEnable`, and the comparison evaluated to true, the depth attachment value z_{a} is set to the sample’s depth value z_{f}. If there is no depth attachment, no value is written.\n\nTo dynamically enable or disable the depth test, call:\n\nValid Usage\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable-None-08971\nAt least one of the following must be true:\n\n    * the `extendedDynamicState` feature is enabled\n\n    * the `shaderObject` feature is enabled\n\n    * the value of VkApplicationInfo::`apiVersion` used to create the VkInstance parent of `commandBuffer` is greater than or equal to Version 1.3\n\nValid Usage (Implicit)\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable-commandBuffer-parameter\n`commandBuffer` must be a valid VkCommandBuffer handle\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable-commandBuffer-recording\n`commandBuffer` must be in the recording state\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable-commandBuffer-cmdpool\nThe `VkCommandPool` that `commandBuffer` was allocated from must support VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT operations\n\n  * VUID-vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable-videocoding\nThis command must only be called outside of a video coding scope\n\nHost Synchronization\n\n  * Host access to `commandBuffer` must be externally synchronized\n\nTo dynamically set the depth write enable, call:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_VERSION_1_3\n    void vkCmdSetDepthWriteEnable(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkBool32                                    depthWriteEnable);`\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state, VK_EXT_shader_object\n    // Equivalent to vkCmdSetDepthWriteEnable\n    void vkCmdSetDepthWriteEnableEXT(\n        VkCommandBuffer                             commandBuffer,\n        VkBool32                                    depthWriteEnable);`\n\n  * `commandBuffer` is the command buffer into which the command will be recorded.\n\n  * `depthWriteEnable` specifies if depth writes are enabled.\n\nThis command sets the depth write enable for subsequent drawing commands when drawing using shader objects, or when the graphics pipeline is created with VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_DEPTH_WRITE_ENABLE set in VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo::`pDynamicStates`. Otherwise, this state is specified by the VkPipelineDepthStencilStateCreateInfo::`depthWriteEnable` value used to create the currently active pipeline.\n## Representative Fragment Test\n\nThe representative fragment test allows implementations to reduce the amount of rasterization and fragment processing work performed for each point, line, or triangle primitive. For any primitive that produces one or more fragments that pass all prior early fragment tests, the implementation may choose one or more “representative” fragments for processing and discard all other fragments. For draw calls rendering multiple points, lines, or triangles arranged in lists, strips, or fans, the representative fragment test is performed independently for each of those primitives. The set of fragments discarded by the representative fragment test is implementation-dependent. In some cases, the representative fragment test may not discard any fragments for a given primitive.\n\nIf the `pNext` chain of VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo includes a `VkPipelineRepresentativeFragmentTestStateCreateInfoNV` structure, then that structure includes parameters controlling the representative fragment test.\n\nThe `VkPipelineRepresentativeFragmentTestStateCreateInfoNV` structure is defined as:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_NV_representative_fragment_test\n    typedef struct VkPipelineRepresentativeFragmentTestStateCreateInfoNV {\n        VkStructureType    sType;\n        const void*        pNext;\n        VkBool32           representativeFragmentTestEnable;\n    } VkPipelineRepresentativeFragmentTestStateCreateInfoNV;`\n\n  * `sType` is a VkStructureType value identifying this structure.\n\n  * `pNext` is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this structure.\n\n  * `representativeFragmentTestEnable` controls whether the representative fragment test is enabled.\n\nIf this structure is not included in the `pNext` chain, `representativeFragmentTestEnable` is considered to be VK_FALSE, and the representative fragment test is disabled.\n\nIf the active fragment shader does not specify the `EarlyFragmentTests` execution mode, the representative fragment shader test has no effect, even if enabled.\n\nValid Usage (Implicit)\n## Sample Counting\n\nOcclusion queries use query pool entries to track the number of samples that pass all the per-fragment tests. The mechanism of collecting an occlusion query value is described in Occlusion Queries.\n\nThe occlusion query sample counter increments by one for each sample with a coverage value of 1 in each fragment that survives all the per-fragment tests, including scissor, exclusive scissor, sample mask, alpha to coverage, stencil, and depth tests.\n\n## Fragment Coverage to Color\n\nThe `VkPipelineCoverageToColorStateCreateInfoNV` structure is defined as:\n    \n    `// Provided by VK_NV_fragment_coverage_to_color\n    typedef struct VkPipelineCoverageToColorStateCreateInfoNV {\n        VkStructureType                                sType;\n        const void*                                    pNext;\n        VkPipelineCoverageToColorStateCreateFlagsNV    flags;\n        VkBool32                                       coverageToColorEnable;\n        uint32_t                                       coverageToColorLocation;\n        VkSampleCountFlags           colorSamples;\n    } VkFramebufferMixedSamplesCombinationNV;`\n\n  * `sType` is a VkStructureType value identifying this structure.\n\n  * `pNext` is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this structure.\n\n  * `coverageReductionMode` is a VkCoverageReductionModeNV value specifying the coverage reduction mode.\n\n  * `rasterizationSamples` is a VkSampleCountFlagBits specifying the number of rasterization samples in the supported combination.\n\n  * `depthStencilSamples` specifies the number of samples in the depth stencil attachment in the supported combination. A value of 0 indicates the combination does not have a depth stencil attachment.\n\n  * `colorSamples` specifies the number of color samples in a color attachment in the supported combination. A value of 0 indicates the combination does not have a color attachment.\n\nValid Usage (Implicit)\n\n  * VUID-VkFramebufferMixedSamplesCombinationNV-sType-sType\n`sType` must be VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FRAMEBUFFER_MIXED_SAMPLES_COMBINATION_NV\n\n  * VUID-VkFramebufferMixedSamplesCombinationNV-pNext-pNext\n`pNext` must be `NULL`\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nLayers & Extensions (Informative) :: Vulkan Documentation Project (https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/appendices/extensions.html)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn29search1\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 weeks ago; Authors creating extensions and layers must follow the mandatory procedures described in the Vulkan Documentation and Extensions document when creating extensions and layers. ...   * Add a property query to determine if a framebuffer writes to depth or stencil aspect does not trigger a write access in the sibling aspect. ...
