Crawled: 4 months ago; # earlydepthstencil\n\n# earlydepthstencil\n\n反馈\n\n## 本文内容\n\n在执行着色器之前强制进行深度模具测试。\n    \n    `earlydepthstencil   \n    `\n\n## 备注\n\n深度模具测试通常在像素处理期间由像素着色器完成。 强制提前深度模具测试会导致在着色器执行之前完成测试;目的是通过剔除/减少/避免不必要的像素处理来提高每个像素的性能。\n\n应用程序可以通过提供 属性来强制早期深度模具测试，或者硬件可以执行早期深度模具测试，前提是未写入深度值，并且着色器中没有作为优化执行无序访问操作。\n\n以下类型的着色器支持此属性：\n\n顶点  | 外壳  | 域  | Geometry  | 像素  | 计算\n--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---\n |  |  |  | x  | \n\n## 相关主题\n\n着色器模型 5 特性\n\n着色器模型 5\n\n\xa0\n\n  * Last updated on 2023-06-13--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nearlydepthstencil - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/ja-jp/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/sm5-attributes-earlydepthstencil)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn30search6\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3.2 years ago; Crawled: last month; # earlydepthstencil\n\n# earlydepthstencil\n\nフィードバック\n\n## この記事の内容\n\nシェーダーを実行する前に深度ステンシル テストを強制します。\n    \n    `earlydepthstencil   \n    `\n\n## 解説\n\n深度ステンシル テストは、通常、ピクセル シェーダーによるピクセル処理中に行われます。 早期深度ステンシル テストを強制すると、シェーダーの実行前にテストが実行されます。この目的は、不要なピクセル処理をカリング/削減/回避することで、ピクセルごとのパフォーマンスを向上させることです。\n\nアプリケーションでは、 属性を指定することで早期深度ステンシル テストを強制できます。また、深度値が書き込まれず、シェーダーで最適化として順序なしのアクセス操作が実行されない場合は、ハードウェアが早期深度ステンシル テストを実行する可能性があります。\n\nこの属性は、次の種類のシェーダーでサポートされています。\n\nVertex  | Hull  | Domain  | ジオメトリ  | ピクセル  | Compute\n--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---\n\n## 関連トピック\n\nシェーダー モデル 5 の属性\n\nシェーダー モデル 5\n\n\n  * Last updated on 2023-06-13--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nearlydepthstencil - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/ko-kr/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/sm5-attributes-earlydepthstencil)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn30search7\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3.2 years ago; Crawled: 4 months ago; # earlydepthstencil\n\n# earlydepthstencil\n\n피드백\n\n## 이 문서의 내용\n\n셰이더가 실행되기 전에 깊이 스텐실 테스트를 강제합니다.\n    \n    `earlydepthstencil   \n    `\n\n## 설명\n\n깊이 스텐실 테스트는 일반적으로 픽셀 셰이더에 의한 픽셀 처리 중에 수행됩니다. 초기 깊이 스텐실 테스트를 강제하면 셰이더 실행 전에 테스트가 수행됩니다. 목적은 불필요한 픽셀 처리를 제거/축소/방지하여 픽셀당 성능을 개선시키는 것입니다.\n\n애플리케이션은 특성을 제공하여 초기 깊이 스텐실 테스트를 강제할 수 있으며, 깊이 값이 작성되지 않고 셰이더에서 최적화로 수행되는 정렬되지 않은 액세스 작업이 없는 경우 하드웨어가 초기 깊이 스텐실 테스트를 실행할 수 있습니다.\n\n이 특성은 다음 형식의 셰이더에서 지원됩니다.\n\n꼭짓점  | Hull  | 도메인  | 기하 도형  | 픽셀  | 컴퓨팅\n--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---\n |  |  |  | x  | \n\n## 관련 항목\n\n셰이더 모델 5 특성\n\n셰이더 모델 5\n\n\xa0\n\n  * Last updated on 2023-06-13--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nearlydepthstencil - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/es-es//windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/sm5-attributes-earlydepthstencil)\n\ue200cite\ue202turn30search8\ue201 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3.2 years ago; ## 🤖 Agent

The established renderer’s encoding is a useful specification oracle here: it treats the three Xenos compare bits as less/equal/greater, handles `NotEqual` separately with unordered floating comparison, and bypasses alpha testing when RT0 was not written. I’m checking whether XenosRecomp can preserve that last condition statically from its output metadata, so the fix doesn’t invent behavior for depth-only shaders.

One specific example is deferred rendering can avoid processing lighting for pixels that fall outside a light’s influence.\nL36: \nL37: Also, this supports Xbox/Windows D3D parity.\nL38: # Detailed Design\nL39: \nL40: The Depth Bounds Test API will be added to D3D12 as an optional feature.\nL41: This feature allows a programmer to discard pixels (or samples) based on a minimum and maximum depth value: if the current depth value in the depth buffer is inclusively within the specified range, then the pixel (or sample) has passed the Depth Bounds Test and is rendered, otherwise the pixel (or sample) has failed the Depth Bounds Test and is discarded.\nL42: It is important to note that this feature is independent of the depth output by a given pixel shader invocation: only the currently stored depth value and the programmer-specified Depth Bounds values are relevant.\nL43: This API will be exposed as a PSO enable/disable toggle in order to support hardware that sets depth buffer read state in the PSO, and Command List method in order to support dynamically changing the Depth Bounds. It will allow the setting of two floating point values: a minimum floating point depth value and a maximum floating point depth value. The runtime will not clamp or validate the input, but implementations may clamp to the range [0,1] if necessary.\nL44: NaNs must be treated as 0, but the runtime will convert NaNs to 0 on behalf of the implementation. If the range is inverted (i.e. min \\max), then implementations must treat the Depth Bounds Test as always failing. The default values are 0 and 1 for the minimum and maximum, respectively.\nL45: The state of the DBT range will persist into and out-of Bundles. This means that a Bundle must inherit the DBT range of the executing Command List, and setting the DBT range in a Bundle will persist on the executing Command List after the Bundle is executed.\nL46: Any Pixel Shader invocation that fails the Depth Bounds Test (i.e. whose stored depth buffer value falls exclusively outside the Depth Bounds range) cannot affect the render target, depth, or stencil buffer. However, UAV writes by a pixel shader invocation that fails the Depth Bounds Test are determined by the ForceEarlyDepthStencil flag.\nL47: When the ForceEarlyDepthStencil flag is present an implementation must perform the Depth/Stencil tests, the Depth Bounds Test, and Depth/Stencil writes before executing the Pixel Shader, which prohibits any external effects (e.g. UAV writes) from the Pixel Shader invocation.\nL48: In the absence of the ForceEartlyDepthStencil flag an implementation may perform optimizations, but must appear to have executed the Depth/Stencil Tests and Depth Bounds Test after the Pixel Shader invocation and must reflect any memory updates (e.g. oDepth and UAV writes) performed by the invocation.\nL49: Note that while a Pixel Shader invocation’s oDepth is honored in the absence of the ForceEarlyDepthStencil flag, the Depth Bounds Test for a given Pixel Shader invocation does not use the depth written by that invocation: it uses the current depth buffer value prior to its own writes.\nL50: When a depth buffer is not bound (e.g. when TIR is enabled), the Depth Bounds Test must always pass. This is consistent with the behavior of the Depth Test in this configuration.\nL51: \nL52: The Depth Bounds Test affects the following queries: Occlusion, Binary Occlusion, and Pipeline Statistics. These queries must exclude counting samples that failed the Depth Bounds Test.\nL53: \nL54: * * *\nL55: # API\nL56: The Depth Stencil State Desc will be revised to include an enable/disable DBT toggle, which will necessitate revising the PSO Desc and Creation API. In order to support fast iterations on pipeline state, we will move away from the existing design that requires a PSO Desc revision and Creation interface/method revision per update, and implement one that is more dynamic: a token stream.\nL57: This design describes the pipeline state in a much more flexible manner and can be extended without revising the CreatePSO interface or method. The API would consist of an enumeration type that describes the following token to parse from the stream.\nL58: * * *\nL59: ## New Create PSO Concepts\nL60: Subobjects will now be the constituent components of a pipeline state object. A pipeline state stream is constructed from a grouping (within a struct) of these subobjects, which from a technical perspective are structs that contain a pair of subobject type enum followed by the respective subobject desc. The D3DX12 stream elements (described later) represent these pairs, and allow short-form construction of custom streams.\nL61: An important note is that the runtime assumes the stream is constructed from structs of enum+desc pairs, which defines the padding expected by the runtime.\nL62: * * *\nL63: ## Stream Padding Assumptions\nL64: As an example of how the runtime assumes the stream is constructed with respect to subobject-internal padding, we can look at a Root Signature subobject:\nL65: \nL66:     `MY_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ROOT_SIGNATURE\nL67:     +0x000 _Type : D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE\nL68:     +0x008 _Inner : Ptr64 ID3D12RootSignature\nL69: \nL70:     sizeof(MY_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ROOT_SIGNATURE) unsigned int64 0x10\nL71:     sizeof(D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE) unsigned int64 4\nL72:     sizeof(ID3D12RootSignature*) unsigned int64 8\nL73:     `\nL74: Simply adding the type and root signature pointer sizes would not account for the padding of four bytes between the enum and pointer, thus the runtime parses this subobject from the stream as a full subobject struct, rather than as a type and pointer separately.\nL75: When subobjects are combined into a stream the parsing code assumes alignas(void) is used for each subobject (if alignas() is unavailable, then an alternative such as unioning the data with a void is a valid workaround). This is necessary because the parsing code requires an enum to be packed tightly against the end of the previous element as determined by sizeof(previous element).\nL76: If an element is not void* aligned, but the subsequent element is, then there will be padding inserted between them and the parser will read that instead of the enum type. Because of this, all helpers are declared as such:\nL77: \nL78:     `template <...>\nL79:     class alignas(void*) CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_SUBOBJECT\nL80:     `\nL81: * * *\nL82: ## Base Create PSO API\nL83: Listed here is the standard D3D12 API exposed to create a PSO. It consists of the subobject type enum, the subobject desc structs (as they exist today), and the device function for CreatePipelineState().\nL84: \nL85:     `typedef struct D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_DESC\nL86:     {\nL87:         SIZE_T SizeInBytes;\nL88:         void* pPipelineStateSubobjectStream;\nL89:     } D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_DESC;\nL90: \nL91:     typedef enum D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE\nL92:     {\nL93:         D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_VS,\nL94:         D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_VS_INLINE,\nL95:         D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_DEPTH_STENCIL,\nL96:         D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_RASTERIZER,\nL97:         ...\nL98:         D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_DEPTH_STENCIL1\nL99:     } D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE;\nL100: \nL101:     // Desc for D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_DEPTH_STENCIL\nL102:     typedef struct D3D12_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC\nL103:     {\nL104:         BOOL DepthEnable;\nL105:         ...\nL106:     } D3D12_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC;\nL107:     // Desc for D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_DEPTH_STENCIL1\nL108:     typedef struct D3D12_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC1\nL109:     {\nL110:         BOOL DepthEnable;\nL111:         ...\nL112:         BOOL DepthBoundsTestEnable;\nL113:     } D3D12_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC1;\nL114: \nL115:     interface ID3D12Device1 : ID3D12Device\nL116:     {\nL117:         ...\nL118:         HRESULT CreatePipelineState(\nL119:             D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_DESC Desc,\nL120:             REFIID riid, // Can be any pipeline interface, provided the pipeline subobjects match\nL121:             void** ppPipelineState\nL122:             );\nL123:     }\nL124:     `\nL125: For any pipeline state subobjects not found in the stream, defaults will be used. Defaults will also be used if an old version of a subobject is found in the stream, e.g. an old DepthStencil State desc would not contain DBT information so the default of disabled would be used. The same CreatePSO validation that exists now will be used.\nL126: \nL127: * * *\nL128: ## D3DX12 Helpers\nL129: \nL130: D3DX12 will be leveraged to create helper classes for developers to more easily construct a pipeline stream. We want to use C++ features, and thus we must put these helpers in D3DX12 rather than the base D3D12 API.\nL131: As a foundation, we will create a set of classes that pair enum with struct that can be combined as members of a struct to form a stream. Note that these are the actual types used to parse the stream and define the padding assumptions detailed earlier. The three examples shown here illustrate the three types of subobjects: a simple D3D12-API POD type, a primitive type, and a Desc that should have defaults.\nL132: \nL133:     `template <typename InnerStructType,\nL134:     D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE Type, typename DefaultArg = InnerStructType> class CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT\nL135:     {\nL136:     private:\nL137:         D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE _Type;\nL138:         InnerStructType _Inner;\nL139: \nL140:     public:\nL141:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT() : _Type(Type), _Inner(DefaultArg()) { }\nL142: \nL143:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT(InnerStructType const& i) : _Type(Type), _Inner(i) { }\nL144:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT& operator=(InnerStructType const& i) { _Inner = i; return *this; }\nL145: \nL146:         operator InnerStructType() { return _Inner; }\nL147: \nL148:     };\nL149: \nL150:     typedef CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT<D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_FLAGS,D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_FLAGS>\nL151:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_FLAGS;\nL152: \nL153:     typedef CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT\\<UINT,D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_NODE_MASK>\nL154:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_NODE_MASK;\nL155: \nL156:     typedef CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_ELEMENT\\<CD3DX12_RASTERIZER_DESC,D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_RASTERIZER,CD3DX12_DEFAULT>\nL157:       CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_RASTERIZER;\nL158: \nL159:     struct MyPSOStream\nL160:     {\nL161:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_FLAGS Flags;\nL162:         CD3DX12_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM_RASTERIZER RasterizerState;\nL163:     };\nL164:     `\nL165: One important note about these classes is that they hide the InnerStructType behind constructors and a cast operator. This can be leveraged in the future when we want to update an InnerStructType (e.g. rasterizer state) but allow backwards compatibility. This would be useful to avoid breaking changes if someone recompiles with the latest header and we’ve updated one of the constituent parts of the full graphics pipeline struct (described later).\nL166: One downside of this is that accessing member data within a stream struct requires a cast, e.g. D3D12_SHADER_BYTECODE(GraphicsPSOStream.VS).pShaderBytecode, although we don’t expect that to be a very common use case since typically the dev will be assigning rather than accessing.\nL486: To version the full stream definitions, e.g. CD3DX12_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_STATE_STREAM, we will replace the old subobject with the latest and no attempt at backwards compatibility of this specific object will be made. We don’t expect the full pipeline streams to be used heavily and the information density cost of keeping around old versions will be high due their lengthy nature.\nL487: If need be, we can add operators/constructors to the subobjects that allow for the new subobject to compile seamlessly against code that is trying to assign the old subobject desc.\nL488: ## DepthBoundsTest API\nL489: \nL490: The DBT range setting API will be exposed as a Graphics Command List method in order to support dynamically changing the Depth Bounds. This requires a new ID3D12GraphicsCommandList interface.\nL491: \nL492:     `interface ID3D12GraphicsCommandList1\nL493:     : ID3D12GraphicsCommandList\nL494:     {\nL495:         ...\nL496:         void OMSetDepthBounds(\nL497:         FLOAT Min,\nL498:         FLOAT Max\nL499:         );\nL500:     }\nL501:     `\nL502: \nL503: The default values are 0 and 1 for the Min and Max, respectively, and NaNs are converted to 0.\nL504: We will add a CheckFeatureSupport query, e.g. D3D12_FEATURE_D3D12_OPTIONS2, to determine whether this feature is supported based on UMD version.\nL505: In addition to the setting of the Depth Bounds, an enable/disable toggle will be added to the PSO in order to support hardware implementations that configure their depth buffer reads in the PSO.\nL506: \nL507:     `// Desc for D3D12_PIPELINE_STATE_SUBOBJECT_TYPE_DEPTH_STENCIL1\nL508:     typedef struct D3D12_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC1\nL509:     {\nL510:         BOOL DepthEnable;\nL511:         ...\nL512:         BOOL DepthBoundsTestEnable;\nL513:     } D3D12_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC1;\nL514:     `\nL515: \nL516: * * *\nL517: # DDI\nL518: \nL519: A new Depth Stencil State Creation and Set Depth Bounds DDI will be added to the set of 3D Command List DDIs. We will use the DDI versioning scheme for a non-breaking build bump change (as detailed in DDIHelper.hpp).\nL520: For the Depth Stencil State Creation DDI:\nL521: \nL522:     `typedef struct D3D12DDI_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC_0011\nL523:     {\nL524:         ...\nL525:         BOOL DepthBoundsTestEnable;\nL526:     } D3D12DDI_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC_0011;\nL527: \nL528:     typedef SIZE_T ( APIENTRY* PFND3D12DDI_CALCPRIVATEDEPTHSTENCILSTATESIZE_0011 )(\nL529:         D3D12DDI_HDEVICE, _In_ CONST D3D12DDI_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC_0011*\nL530:     );\nL531: \nL532:     typedef VOID ( APIENTRY* PFND3D12DDI_CREATEDEPTHSTENCILSTATE_0011 )(\nL533:         D3D12DDI_HDEVICE, _In_ CONST D3D12DDI_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC_0011*,\nL534:         D3D12DDI_HDEPTHSTENCILSTATE );\nL535: \nL536:     typedef struct D3D12DDI_DEVICE_FUNCS_CORE_0011\nL537:     {\nL538:         ...\nL539:         PFND3D12DDI_CALCPRIVATEDEPTHSTENCILSTATESIZE_0011 pfnCalcPrivateDepthStencilStateSize;\nL540:         PFND3D12DDI_CREATEDEPTHSTENCILSTATE_0011 pfnCreateDepthStencilState;\nL541:         ...\nL542:     } D3D12DDI_DEVICE_FUNCS_CORE_0011;\nL543:     `\nL544: For the Set Depth Bounds DDI:\nL545: \nL546:     `typedef VOID ( APIENTRY* PFND3D12DDI_OM_SETDEPTHBOUNDS_0011 )(\nL547:         D3D12DDI_HCOMMANDLIST, FLOAT Min, FLOAT Max);\nL548: \nL549:     typedef struct D3D12DDI_COMMAND_LIST_FUNCS_3D_0011 {\nL550:         ...\nL551:         PFND3D12DDI_OM_SETDEPTHBOUNDS pfnOMSetDepthBounds;\nL552:     } D3D12DDI_COMMAND_LIST_FUNCS_3D_0011;\nL553:     `\nL554: \nL555: The default values are 0 and 1 for the minimum and maximum, respectively.\nL556: A new D3D12DDICAPS_TYPE_D3D12_OPTIONS query will be added to the GetCaps DDI to retrieve support information.\nL557: \nL558: * * *\nL559: # Runtime Code\nL560: \nL561: The implementation work in the runtime will consist of versioning the device interface to add the new PSO Creation API implementation and versioning command list interface to add the DBT range setting method. Ideally, the DBT range setting API would have one implementation that does a simple DDI call, and one that does a version/caps check and removes the command list when the OMSetDepthBounds DDI is not supported.\nL562: The existing command list v-table design does not support optional DDIs. Therefore, we need to add the ability for the DDI-filling code to query the runtime to provide implementations for optional DDIs that a driver doesn’t want to support, e.g. the set for DBT range. The code would consist of the UpdateGlobalDDITable function using the recursive template parameter parsing mechanism to call a templated function that looks like this (in pseudo code):\nL563: \nL564:     `template<TableType TT, typename T>\nL565:     FillUnsupportedDDIs(T& table)\nL566:     {\nL567:         if (TT == command_list && DBTNotSupported())\nL568:         {\nL569:             __if_exists(T::pfnSetDBTRange)\nL570:             {\nL571:                 Table.pfnSetDBTRange = pfnSetDBTRangeUnsupported;\nL572:             }\nL573:         }\nL574:     }\nL575:     `\nL576: ## Runtime Validation\nL577: \nL578: The API validation in the SDK layers will consist of a min-max inversion check: min \\max generates a warning message when SDK layers are present.\nL579: \nL580: The runtime will convert NaNs to 0.\nL581: \nL582: * * *\nL583: \nL584: ## SDK Layers Validation\nL585: \nL586: The API validation in the SDK layers will consist of a min-max inversion check: min > max generates a warning message when SDK layers are present.\nL587: \nL588: * * *\nL589: ## D3DDbg Considerations\nL590: \nL591: The D3DDbg windbg extension is able understand PSOs Descs. We will update the SmallDepthStencilStateDesc to the latest (with the Depth Bounds).\nL592: \nL593: * * *\nL594: \nL595: # Testing\nL596: \nL597: * * *\nL598: ## Functional\nL599: \nL600: Functional tests will be written using the TAEF framework, use driver-type WARP, integrate into D3DFunc_12_Core.dll, and verify matching parameters at the DDI. This consists of using the TAEF mocking functionality to check the DDI parameters passed to WARP. These tests will be added to the RI-TP automatically by being included in D3DFunc_12_Core.dll.\nL601: \nL602: To enumerate the functional test cases:\nL603:   * Verify min-max inversion validation, the following must still call WARP but generate a warning message\nL604: \nL605:     * Min > Max\nL606:   * Verify the runtime calls WARP with matching values, and generates no error messages\nL607: \nL608:     * Min > 0, Max < 1, Min < Max\nL609:   * Verify the runtime converts NaNs to Zero, calls WARP with Zeros, and generates no error messages\nL610: \nL611:     * Min = NaN, Max = NaN\nL612: \nL613: * * *\nL614: ## Conformance\nL615: \nL616: Conformance tests will be written using the TAEF framework, use driver-type hardware, integrate into D3DConf_12_core.dll, and verify driver and hardware behavior when Depth Bounds are set. These tests must be integrated into the HLK (which requires Display Gatherer work), as well as support being dropped to IHVs as a private binary.\nL617: \nL618: The important hardware-behaviors to test are:\nL619: \nL620:   * the programmer-specified depth range is properly considered exclusive wrt to discarding\nL621:   * DBT-failing pixel shader invocations do not affect a bound RT or depth stencil, and do not affect UAVs when ForceEarlyDepthStencil is enabled\nL622: \nL623:   * Depth Bounds Test affects Occlusion, Binary Occlusion, and Pipeline Statistics queries.\nL624: \nL625:   * Depth Bounds Test Behavior with respect to Bundles\nL626: \nL627: The conformance test cases are:\nL628:   1. Verify Depth Bounds Test correctly limits writes to the Render Target as well as UAVs\nL629:      * Bind a zeroed 1x5 RT with depth buffer, and a zeroed UINT-per-pixel sized UAV.\nL630:      * Enable ForceEarlyDepthStencil flag\nL631:      * Set the Depth Bounds to range [0.3,0.6]\nL632:      * Fill depth buffer with values: 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 1\nL633:      * 0 < Min, so must be discarded\nL634:      * 0.3 == Min, so must affect memory\nL635:      * Min < 0.5 < Max, so must affect memory\nL636:      * 0.6 == Max, so must affect memory\nL637:      * 1 > Max, so must be discarded - Render to all pixels\nL638:      * PS must output <1,1,1,1> to RT and 1 to the corresponding UAV address - Ensure only the pixels at <0,1>,<0,2>,<0,3> updated memory for both the RT and UAV - Ensure occlusion query reports 3 pixels passed - Ensure binary occlusion query reports true (pixels passed) - Ensure Pipeline Statistics PSInvocations reports 3 pixels\nL639:   2. Run test #1 but set Depth Bounds via a Bundle\nL640:      * Expect same result as #1\nL641:   3. Run test #1 with no depth buffer bound\nL642:      * Expect no pixels updated, and matching query data\nL643:   4. Run test #1 with no depth buffer bound and Depth Bounds set to range [0, 1]\nL644:      * Expect all pixels updated, and matching query data\nL645:   5. Run test #1 with Depth Bounds set to range [-FLT_MAX, FLT_MAX]\nL646:      * Expect all pixels updated, and matching query data\nL647:   6. Run test #1 with Depth Bounds set to range [FLT_MAX, -FLT_MAX]\nL648:      * Expect no pixels updated (due to min-max inversion), and matching query data\nL649: * * *\nL650: # Change Log\nL651: \nL652:   * V1.0 – First Draft\nL653: \nL654:   * V1.1 – Updated behavior wrt to external effects (e.g. UAV writes) when the DBT fails: before external effects were prohibited, now they are prohibited or not based on early or late depth stencil.\nL655: \nL656:   * V1.2 – Updated behavior when depth buffer is not bound: before DBT could be enabled and depth reads return 0, now it must always pass (which is now consistent with the Depth Test).\nL657:   * V1.3 – Removed note about Conservative oDepth since it was more confusing than helpful\nL658: \nL659: This site is open source. \ue200cite\ue20225†Improve this page†github.com\ue201 .\n'}

## 🤖 Agent

Research complete; no repository edits, Git, or pseudocode used.

Key finding: the alpha-test failure has two coupled causes.

- Native runtime only specializes `GreaterEqual` at [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:6318).
- XenosRecomp inserts an alpha-test `clip` into every pixel shader at [shader_recompiler.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/tools/XenosRecomp/XenosRecomp/shader_recompiler.cpp:2474), but also marks non-depth-exporting pixel shaders `[earlydepthstencil]` at [shader_recompiler.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/tools/XenosRecomp/XenosRecomp/shader_recompiler.cpp:1927).

A DXC/SPIR-V probe confirmed those modules contain both `EarlyFragmentTests` and `OpKill`. Early depth/stencil writes may therefore occur before alpha rejection, producing invisible depth-writing texels—the exact downstream behavior that can occlude lights or translucent objects.

The established shared Vulkan renderer already models this correctly:

- Packs the full three-bit Xenos comparison at [command_processor.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/vulkan/command_processor.cpp:6308).
- Implements all eight comparisons at [spirv_translator_rb.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/pipeline/shader/spirv_translator_rb.cpp:490).
- Disables early mode when coverage depends on alpha at [pipeline_cache.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:990).

Proper implementation design:

- Preserve specialization bit `0x2` as alpha-test enable.
- Reserve bits 8–10 for the three-bit comparison function: function mask `0x700`, complete capability mask `0x702`. These were verified by `/tmp/alpha_spec_layout.py`.
- Implement `Never`, ordered less/equal/greater combinations, unordered `NotEqual`, and `Always`.
- For `NotEqual`, use `isnan(alpha) || isnan(reference) || alpha != reference`; DXC maps plain HLSL `!=` to ordered-not-equal, unlike the shared renderer’s `OpFUnordNotEqual`.
- Use `clip(alphaPass ? 1.0f : -1.0f)` so the same source remains valid for AIR/Metal.
- Only emit the test for shaders declaring color target zero.
- Generate two SPIR-V variants for alpha-capable pixel shaders:
  - Early variant for disabled or `Always`.
  - Late variant without `EarlyFragmentTests` for enabled non-`Always`.
- Extend stock and override cache entries with late-variant offsets/pointers, load and destroy both modules, then select the variant during pipeline creation. The existing pipeline key already contains alpha enable/function.
- Update all alpha-capable overrides and their manifest masks from `0x2` to `0x702`.

After generator changes, XenosRecomp must manually regenerate [shader_cache.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/LibertyRecompLib/shader/shader_cache.cpp:1).
